note: Topical anti-TNF biologics (tanfanercept/HL036, licaminlimab = ESBA105/OCS-02) in dry eye: a desiccating-stress mouse and a spontaneous canine KCS model predicted sign benefit that two Phase 3 trials did not show; rabbit ocular-PK predictions held in humans; a TNFR1-genotype responder claim is the live patient-level test.
label: Dry eye (anti-TNF)

engagement.note: Topical HL036 concentrated in cornea/anterior segment and eliminated ocular-surface TNF-α in desiccating-stress mice; no patient TNF-α engagement readout has been published.
engagement.short: HL036 clears ocular-surface TNF-α in mice
engagement.quote: HL036 concentration was significantly higher in cornea and anterior segment than etanercept and effectively eliminated TNF-α on ocular surfaces.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (PMID 24052636); quote verbatim in the abstract.
engagement.reason: No patient TNF-α engagement readout published
engagement.judgement: The only patient-side target readout in the class (conjunctival TNFα/IL1β/IL8 mRNA in the licaminlimab Phase 2, Donnenfeld 2024, doi:10.1097/ICO.0000000000003510) was retracted in October 2024 (notice doi:10.1097/ICO.0000000000003640), so it cannot carry a status. Thiel 2013 measured ESBA105 exposure in aqueous humour, not TNF-α neutralisation; it sits in the dose cell. Engagement pools both modalities, so one track covers the cell.

engagement.model: Aged C57BL/6 mouse, spontaneous age-related dry eye (tanfanercept 0.25% eye drops, 8 weeks)
engagement.confidence_note: Quote is the Figure 5 title in the PMC author manuscript (NIHMS1930421). Tear washings pooled from four eyes per sample, n = 8-10 per arm, Mann-Whitney. The paper states it did not measure tanfanercept concentration in conjunctiva or lacrimal gland, so there is no tissue-exposure readout to compare.
engagement.note: The aged mouse's PD readout is a multiplex tear-cytokine panel; no tanfanercept-dosed human tear-cytokine or ocular-surface TNF-alpha measurement has been published.
engagement.short: Tear cytokines fell in aged mice
engagement.quote: Topical treatment with tanfanercept decreases inflammatory cytokines in tears.
engagement.judgement: Downstream readout (tear cytokines, not free TNF-alpha or a direct occupancy measure). Nobody has reported tear or conjunctival cytokines, or ocular-surface TNF-alpha, in tanfanercept-dosed people (the checker found none in Dong 2022, VELOS or Shettle 2022 either), so the comparison is untested. No dose or safety entries: the paper states no exposure target and makes no tolerability claim for the drops.

dose.model: Rabbit topical ocular PK (ESBA105 eye drops)
dose.note: Topical ESBA105 reached therapeutic concentrations in rabbit aqueous and vitreous, with systemic exposure 25,000-fold below the same dose given i.v.
dose.short: Rabbit eye drops reach therapeutic levels
dose.quote: After topical administration to the eye, ESBA105 quickly reaches therapeutic concentrations in all ocular compartments.
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (PMID 18757508); quote verbatim. Companion paper Ottiger 2009 (doi:10.1167/iovs.08-2372, PMID 18757511) mapped the corneal and scleral penetration routes in the same rabbit system.
dose.judgement: Epub 2008-08-29, print IOVS February 2009; v3 rule 6 takes the earliest public date, so the track opens in 2008 (v2 used 2009). ESBA105 is the molecule later named licaminlimab/OCS-02 (scFv, antibody modality).

dose.model: Rabbit topical ocular PK (ESBA105 eye drops)
dose.note: Topical ESBA105 reached human aqueous-humour levels 96- to 359-fold above intraocular TNF-α, the therapeutic level the rabbit predicted; vitreous was undetectable in 5 of 6.
dose.quote: These results demonstrate that the topically applied single-chain antibody fragment ESBA105 penetrated into the anterior chamber of the human eye at therapeutic levels.
dose.confidence_note: Abstract only (Ophthalmology, paywalled; PMID 23490328); the abstract never mentions the rabbit data, so comparison_stated is false and the pairing is mine. Subjects were otherwise-healthy cataract-surgery patients (NCT00820014, no results posted), not dry-eye patients.
dose.reason: Human aqueous levels matched rabbit prediction
dose.judgement: Healthy-volunteer PK counts for dose under v3, and the cataract cohorts are effectively that for a dry-eye context, so subjects is healthy_volunteers. The rabbit prediction held anteriorly (aqueous 96–359× molar excess over TNF-α) and failed posteriorly (vitreous undetectable in 5/6 after 8 drops/day); for an ocular-surface disease the anterior half is the relevant one, so same with direction_only rather than partial. Under the dose table the target was reached and the drug then hit its Phase 2 symptom primary (licaminlimab, Shettle 2022, p=0.041), which keeps the cell same; RELIEF 2024 reported sign effects without a stated primary-endpoint result and the programme continues (PREDICT-1, NCT07548632, started 2026-04), so no 'reached, failed, abandoned' downgrade applies yet. The registry entry NCT00820014 states the animal-to-human framing ('In animal experiments, ESBA105 was shown to efficiently penetrate...') but posts no results, so it is not used as the source.
dose.magnitude_basis: intraocular ESBA105 concentration relative to a therapeutic (TNF-α-neutralising) level

dose.note: Topical HL036 reached higher corneal and anterior-segment concentrations than etanercept in mice; no human ocular or systemic PK for tanfanercept has been published.
dose.short: Mouse ocular exposure; no human PK published
dose.quote: HL036 concentration was significantly higher in cornea and anterior segment than etanercept and effectively eliminated TNF-α on ocular surfaces.
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (PMID 24052636). Tanfanercept's Phase 1 (NCT02717208, 2016) has no posted or published results.
dose.judgement: Dose is split by modality in a two-modality tile. Tanfanercept (an engineered TNFR1 fragment, protein modality) was never put through the rabbit PK track; its only exposure prediction is the mouse distribution result, and no human exposure or occupancy target was ever stated or measured in public, so the 'reached, failed' row of the dose table cannot be applied and the protein track stays untested rather than contra-derived-from-efficacy. VELOS-4 (NCT06400589) is suspended for a 'logistical issue', not formally abandoned.

efficacy.note: Topical, not systemic, HL036 reduced corneal erosion and restored goblet cells in desiccating-stress mice: a corneal-sign prediction.
efficacy.quote: Corneal erosion and goblet cell counts were improved only with topically applied etanercept and HL036.
efficacy.judgement: The model's readout is a corneal sign (erosion, goblet cells) plus cytokine suppression; it predicts nothing about symptoms. Scopolamine-plus-airflow is the standard desiccating-stress induction; the abstract says only 'DE-induced C57BL/6 mice', so the exact induction was not verified.

efficacy.note: In 29 dogs with naturally occurring KCS, topical HL036 improved clinical-sign scores and Schirmer values and beat 1% cyclosporine on total sign score.
efficacy.short: HL036 beats cyclosporine in dogs with KCS
efficacy.quote: Our findings suggest that topical aqueous HL036 is well-tolerated and more effective than 1% CsA for treating naturally occurring canine KCS.
efficacy.judgement: A different system from the mouse (spontaneous disease, outbred species, active comparator) making a different prediction (superiority to an approved dry-eye drug on signs and tear production), so under this run's track-identity rule it is its own track rather than a strengthening entry on the mouse track.

efficacy.note: VELOS-2 (n=637) missed both co-primaries: inferior corneal staining LS-mean difference 0.08 (p=0.187) and ocular discomfort 0.05 (p=0.555); VELOS-3 repeated the miss in 2023.
efficacy.quote: Coprimary Endpoint: Change From Baseline in Inferior Corneal Fluorescein Staining Score to Day 57 (Pre- to Post-CAE) — 0.25% HL036 vs Placebo: LS Mean Difference 0.08 (95% CI -0.04 to 0.21), P-Value 0.1871
efficacy.confidence_note: The registry record has no prose sentence; the quote is assembled from the posted outcome title and statistical-analysis fields (verified via the ClinicalTrials.gov v2 API, results first posted 2022-04-14). No peer-reviewed VELOS-2 or VELOS-3 paper was found.
efficacy.judgement: The mouse readout is a corneal sign, and the corneal-staining co-primary failed in both pivotal trials, so the model's prediction was contradicted; no source puts the mouse result beside the VELOS data (comparison_stated false, model_src Ji 2013). The miss was already visible in the Phase 2s: VELOS-1 (NCT03334539, results posted 2022-01-26) missed both registered co-primaries (ICSS p=0.29/0.34, ODS p=0.15/0.23) and the China Phase 2 (Dong 2022) reported its ICSS primary at p=0.65 under a positive title; the sponsor's 'Phase 2 signal' was a secondary central-staining score. VELOS-2 is used as the source because it is the pivotal record. Licaminlimab's Phase 2 symptom hit (Shettle 2022, global ocular discomfort p=0.041) is a symptom endpoint the mouse does not read out, so it neither confirms nor rescues the sign prediction. Harbour's China Phase 3 (NCT04633213, completed 2022-08) has no posted results. VELOS-4 (NCT06400589, Schirmer primary) is suspended.

patient_trials.quote: Coprimary Endpoint: Change From Baseline in Inferior Corneal Staining Score to Day 57 (Pre-CAE) — 0.25% HL036 vs Placebo: LS Mean Difference 0.12 (95% CI -0.10 to 0.35), P-Value 0.2883

The tanfanercept treatment group showed improvement in ICSS pre- to post-CAE change from baseline scores when compared to placebo (- 0.61 ± 0.11 and - 0.54 ± 0.11, respectively; mean difference = 0.07, p = 0.65).
Change From Baseline in Central Corneal Staining Score (CCSS) at Day 57 — Tanfanercept vs Placebo: LS Mean Difference -0.03 (95% CI -0.214 to 0.157), P-Value 0.764

efficacy.note: Dogs predicted sign and Schirmer benefit beyond cyclosporine; in VELOS-2 tanfanercept did not beat placebo on corneal staining (p=0.187) or discomfort (p=0.555).
efficacy.short: Dog sign benefit; Phase 3 flat vs placebo
efficacy.quote: Coprimary Endpoint: Change From Baseline in Inferior Corneal Fluorescein Staining Score to Day 57 (Pre- to Post-CAE) — 0.25% HL036 vs Placebo: LS Mean Difference 0.08 (95% CI -0.04 to 0.21), P-Value 0.1871
efficacy.confidence_note: Same registry source and composite quote as the mouse-track entry. The dog study had no placebo arm (HL036 vs 1% CsA, both improved from baseline), so the superiority-to-CsA prediction was never directly tested in patients; the contra rests on the sign prediction failing against placebo.
efficacy.reason: Both sign models missed; Phase 3 flat
efficacy.judgement: Scored on the same VELOS-2 record because the dog prediction (sign improvement, more than an approved comparator) is at least as strong as the mouse one and the human sign endpoint did not move at all. VELOS-3's Schirmer secondary (reported p=0.002 in trade press, not verified in the registry) is the one patient datum pointing the dog's way; it is a secondary and does not change a primary-endpoint call.

efficacy.model: TNFR1 rs1800693 genotype responder analysis (licaminlimab Phase 2)
efficacy.note: Prospectively specified exploratory pharmacogenomics of the 2011 licaminlimab Phase 2 (NCT01338610) associated TNFR1 SNP rs1800693 with discomfort response; paper later retracted at authors' request.
efficacy.quote: The pharmacogenomic analysis was a prospectively specified exploratory objective of the study.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (PMID 38416549, epub 2024-02-28). Retracted 2024-10-01 (PMID 39225356); the retraction notice was not read this run (the v2 checker reported it as author-requested, data deemed exploratory pending RELIEF, with no error or misconduct stated). The task's '2021 Phase 2b' date for this claim could not be verified: no 2021 or 2022 public source was found; the earliest verifiable public record is this paper.
efficacy.judgement: A human-genetic model at patient level: it predicts which dry-eye patients respond, not whether the class works. The association was derived from trial data, so this first entry is the model's construction, not a retrodiction; the first prospective test is the next entry. Population for this track is TNFR1-genotype carriers; the tile population stays Unselected.

efficacy.model: TNFR1 rs1800693 genotype responder analysis (licaminlimab Phase 2)
efficacy.note: RELIEF Phase 2b (n=122): the prespecified TNFR1-genotype subgroup (n=23) showed a significant inferior corneal staining effect at Day 43 (-0.59, CI -1.165 to -0.017); no primary-endpoint result stated.
efficacy.quote: Improvements in multiple sign efficacy endpoints were observed in full population and with predictive and more pronounced effects in the TNFR1 genetic biomarker population as identified in prior successful Phase 2 symptoms trial
efficacy.confidence_note: Tier 5 sponsor release (GlobeNewswire, 2024-06-10) read in full; NCT05896670 has no posted results and no publication was found, and the registry primary is a list of sign endpoints 'at various time points' rather than one named endpoint. The subgroup result is one sign endpoint at one visit in 23 patients, with no carrier-vs-non-carrier test reported; the model paper it rests on was retracted four months later.
efficacy.judgement: The release itself puts the prior Phase 2 genotype finding beside the new trial result, so comparison_stated is true. Scored same with source_calls_it partial: in direction the prediction held (carriers showed the larger, significant sign effect), but the full-population primary is not reported as met, the subgroup is tiny, and a prespecified subgroup is not a randomised genotype comparison. Not a retrodiction: the subgroup was prespecified before unmasking. The decisive prospective test is PREDICT-1 (NCT07548632, Phase 2b/3, started 2026-04-16, 176 randomised, primary = global ocular discomfort at Day 29 in TNFR1-genotype patients, topline expected around year-end 2026), listed below without status. The task called RELIEF the '2023/2024 Phase 3'; it is registered as Phase 2b.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: sign-endpoint treatment effect in TNFR1-genotype carriers versus the full population

patient_trials.quote: The trial also evaluated the efficacy and safety of licaminlimab in a subpopulation of subjects with a TNFR1-related genotype as prespecified in the protocol.
A Clinical Study Evaluating Licaminlimab for Dry Eye Disease

efficacy.model: Aged C57BL/6 mouse, spontaneous age-related dry eye (tanfanercept 0.25% eye drops, 8 weeks)
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read from the PMC author manuscript (PMC10812879, NIHMS1930421, 'unedited manuscript'); quote is from that version, not the publisher PDF. Europe PMC: epub 2023-08-25, print Ocul Surf 30:119-128 (Oct 2023). Tanfanercept 0.25% supplied by HanAll under an MTA; the paper reports no corneal-staining, tear-production or symptom-proxy readout for the drug arm.
efficacy.note: Independent lab (de Paiva): eight weeks of tanfanercept drops restored goblet cells, cut tear cytokines and lacrimal B-cell foci in 12-14-month mice.
efficacy.short: Aged mouse: tanfanercept restores goblet cells
efficacy.quote: Despite these limitations, our results suggest that inhibition of TNF may improve age-related dry eye disease and decrease the formation of ectopic lymphoid structures in the lacrimal glands.
efficacy.judgement: Its own track under this run's identity rule: a spontaneous, inflammaging-driven model (lacrimal-gland ectopic lymphoid structures, 12-14-month females, 8-week dosing) is a different system from the acute desiccating-stress mouse of Ji 2013, and it was the first and only test of a member drug in aged mice. Class-level: it predicts that topical TNF blockade helps age-related dry eye, not who responds. Opens untested at first use; the comparison with the VELOS trials is the next entry.

efficacy.model: Aged C57BL/6 mouse, spontaneous age-related dry eye (tanfanercept 0.25% eye drops, 8 weeks)
efficacy.confidence_note: Paired by the drafter: Kelagere 2023 cites only the 2019 VELOS-1 ARVO abstract as 'positive results' and says tanfanercept is 'currently in Phase III'; it does not mention VELOS-2 or VELOS-3. Registry quote is the same composite of posted outcome fields the checker verified on the mouse track (results first posted 2022-04-14). The model's readouts (goblet cell density, tear cytokines, lacrimal foci, marginal-zone B cells) were not VELOS endpoints; the mismatch is scored on the model's stated efficacy claim. Experiment dates are not given in the paper; the retrodiction flag rests on publication (2023-08-25) post-dating both misses.
efficacy.note: Aged-mouse benefit was published after VELOS-2 and VELOS-3 had missed their corneal-staining and symptom primaries; the model reproduced neither miss.
efficacy.quote: Coprimary Endpoint: Change From Baseline in Inferior Corneal Fluorescein Staining Score to Day 57 (Pre- to Post-CAE) — 0.25% HL036 vs Placebo: LS Mean Difference 0.08 (95% CI -0.04 to 0.21), P-Value 0.1871
efficacy.judgement: Retrodiction: the VELOS-2 ICSS co-primary miss was public from HanAll's 2020-01-21 press conference (release dated 2020-01-28: 'did not meet the primary endpoint of ICSS'), the registry posted 2022-04-14, and VELOS-3 (NCT05109702) missed CCSS and eye-dryness primaries in a 2023-05-23 release before this paper appeared on 2023-08-25, so the aged mouse was run with the clinical answer already known. It predicted benefit and the drug had failed twice on placebo-controlled sign and symptom primaries: a retrodiction that did not reproduce the human data is contra, never retro (decision 10). Dated 2023 because the comparison is public only once the model side is. One drug's contra sets the track. Harbour's China Phase 3 (NCT04633213, n=577, total corneal staining primary, completed 2022-08-07) has no posted results and only an interim 'continue' release, so it neither adds to nor rescues the call. Population stays Unselected: VELOS enrolled adults with dry eye of any cause (mean age about 60), which contains the age-related phenotype the mouse models, and no age-stratified result is posted.

patient_trials.quote: Change From Baseline in Central Corneal Staining Score (CCSS) at Day 57 — Tanfanercept vs Placebo: LS Mean Difference -0.03 (95% CI -0.214 to 0.157), P-Value 0.764
Coprimary Endpoint: Change From Baseline in Inferior Corneal Staining Score to Day 57 (Pre-CAE) — 0.25% HL036 vs Placebo: LS Mean Difference 0.12 (95% CI -0.10 to 0.35), P-Value 0.2883

safety.model: Rabbit topical ocular PK (systemic exposure margin)
safety.note: Rabbit topical PK predicted negligible systemic anti-TNF exposure from eye drops; no GLP ocular toxicology for the class has been published.
safety.quote: Systemic exposure after topical administration is 25,000-fold lower than exposure after i.v. injection of the identical cumulative daily dose.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (PMID 18757508); quote verbatim. The study has no toxicology endpoints; its only safety-relevant output is the systemic-exposure margin.
safety.judgement: The harm this margin speaks to is systemic TNF blockade (infection risk), a platform harm of topical delivery, so under the modality split it is scored on the antibody side; the protein side is carried by the dog track. Year 2008 by v3 rule 6 (epub 2008-08-29).

safety.model: Rabbit topical ocular PK (systemic exposure margin)
safety.note: After up to 8 drops/day, ESBA105 was detectable in 17/55 pre-operative sera and 0/19 a day later; treatment-emergent AEs identical to placebo (2 eye irritations each).
safety.short: Serum transient, AEs same as placebo
safety.quote: ESBA105 was detected in 17 of 55 preoperative serum samples but no longer detectable in serum 1 day after surgery (0 of 19 samples).
safety.confidence_note: Abstract only (PMID 23490328); the paper does not compare with the rabbit data (comparison_stated false). Serum concentrations are not given in the abstract, so the 25,000-fold margin cannot be checked numerically: direction_only.
safety.judgement: Same rule as the dose cell: the first human systemic-exposure result for the product is this cataract-surgery cohort, so the track turns same in 2013 rather than at the 2022 dry-eye paper (the v2 draft split the two cells on this point; one rule now applies to both). The population is another indication, so imported_from is the cataract MONDO id and subjects is healthy_volunteers as in the dose cell.

safety.note: Six weeks of topical HL036 (0.2–5 mg/mL) in 19 dogs with KCS produced no severe adverse reactions; the only published tolerability prediction for tanfanercept.
safety.quote: No severe adverse reactions were noted in either group.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (PMID 29634381); quote verbatim. Tanfanercept's IND toxicology is unpublished.
safety.judgement: Protein-modality safety track. The dog study is tolerability in diseased eyes, not GLP toxicology, so the prediction is narrow: no serious local harm at up to 5 mg/mL twice daily.

safety.note: Eight weeks of 0.25% tanfanercept in 100 Chinese dry-eye patients: no serious AEs; VELOS-2 serious AEs 5/318 vs 4/319 on placebo, none ocular.
safety.short: No serious AEs in patients, as in dogs
safety.quote: Tanfanercept was well tolerated with no serious adverse events occurring during the study.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (PMID 35192105, open access PMC9314282); the paper does not mention the dog study (comparison_stated false). VELOS-2 serious-AE counts are from the registry (results posted 2022-04-14); VELOS-3 posted 0/130 vs 1/130.
safety.judgement: Dong 2022 (epub 2022-02-22) is the earliest peer-reviewed tolerability record for tanfanercept in dry-eye patients and precedes the VELOS-2 registry posting by seven weeks, so it sets the year; the registry counts corroborate. The dog prediction was narrow and held; nothing the dog could have shown (local irritation, infection) appeared beyond instillation-site discomfort seen equally on placebo.

safety.model: Rabbit topical ocular PK (systemic exposure margin)
safety.note: In severe-DED patients on licaminlimab 60 mg/mL for 6 weeks, serum drug was mostly undetectable (max 8.47 ng/mL), with no IOP change and no safety issues.
safety.quote: Serum licaminlimab was undetectable in most patients; the maximum concentration observed was 8.47 ng/mL.
safety.confidence_note: Open-access abstract read (PMID 35821785, PMC9271287); quote verbatim. The paper compares serum levels with systemic anti-TNF agents, not with the rabbit data (comparison_stated false). Trial NCT01338610 (Alcon, 2011–12; results posted 2013-04-19) posts no serum PK and serious AEs 0 in all arms.
safety.reason: Minimal systemic exposure held in patients
safety.judgement: Strengthening entry: the same prediction confirmed in the context's own population, a decade after the trial ran. Licaminlimab is ESBA105 renamed (Novartis/Alcon, then Oculis OCS-02), so product_in_model is true. RELIEF 2024 adds ocular TEAEs 11.5% vs 10.2% on vehicle and no serious ocular AEs (sponsor release).
